statement: If a random variable X is independent of Y and also independent of Z, then X is independent of the pair (Y,Z), and hence of any function of the pair such as Y+Z.
ground_truth_witness: Let Y and Z be independent uniform {0,1} bits and let X = Y XOR Z. The joint pmf puts mass 1/4 on each of (x,y,z) = (0,0,0), (1,0,1), (1,1,0), (0,1,1). Every one of the pairs (X,Y), (X,Z), (Y,Z) is independent, yet X is a deterministic function of (Y,Z): P(X=0,Y=0,Z=0) = 1/4 differs from P(X=0)P(Y=0,Z=0) = 1/8. In particular X is not independent of Y+Z, since P(X=0 | Y+Z=0) = 1 while P(X=0) = 1/2.
reference_authority: published counterexample (book-cited), verified per partB_feasibility records
book_citation: J. M. Stoyanov, Counterexamples in Probability, Wiley, 1987 (3rd ed., Dover, 2013); sections on independence of random events/variables (Bernstein-type triples: pairwise independence without mutual independence); example number not pinned from freely available sources.
